question: What documents do I need for my resident permit application at ACity?
answer: You need: (1) Recent School Fees Payment Receipt, (2) Admission Letter, (3) 2 Passport Pictures, (4) International Passport, and (5) Photocopy of your Non-Citizen Ghana Card. Submit these to the SCA office within the announced submission window.
keywords: resident permit documents requirements SCA international

question: How much does a resident permit cost for international students at ACity?
answer: Costs for 2025–2026: ECOWAS nationals without Ghana Card – GHC 500; with Ghana Card – GHC 400. Non-ECOWAS nationals without Ghana Card – GHC 560; with Ghana Card – GHC 460. All applicants also pay an Administrative Fee of GHC 200. Late penalty: ECOWAS – GHC 200, Non-ECOWAS – GHC 300.
keywords: resident permit cost fee ECOWAS Ghana Card administrative penalty

question: When is the deadline to submit resident permit documents?
answer: For Semester 2 (January 2026), the first deadline was 28 January – 10 February 2026. A second deadline may be set later in the semester. No applications are accepted after the stated deadlines. Submit to the SCA office — documents can be brought directly to SCA during the open window.
keywords: resident permit deadline submission January February SCA

question: How do I collect my resident permit after processing?
answer: Once your resident permit is ready, the International Students Representative will notify you. You then collect it in person from the SCA office. Watch your WhatsApp group and email for the notification.
keywords: resident permit collection SCA pick up

question: How much does it cost to get a Ghana Card as an international student?
answer: New Ghana Card registration for non-citizens costs $120 (requires valid passport or birth certificate). Renewal of an expired card costs $60 (requires expired card and residence permit). Locations near campus: The Gulf House in Shiashie, and CalBank on Independence Avenue.
keywords: Ghana Card cost fee registration renewal international student location

question: What USD to GHS exchange rate does ACity Finance use for fee payments?
answer: Finance updates the rate each week. Rates used in 2025–2026 ranged from USD 1 = GHS 12.25 to GHS 13.00. USD 1 = NGN 1,400–1,550 for Nigerian students. Always check the latest rate communicated by the International Students Representative or Finance before making payment, as it changes weekly.
keywords: exchange rate USD GHS cedis naira Finance payment weekly

question: How much are SRC dues for students at ACity?
answer: SRC dues are $50 per semester (from Semester 2 2025–2026 onward). In Semester 1 2025, students were invoiced $35, but many paid $50 in error — Finance refunded the $15 difference to affected students. The official rate going forward is $50.
keywords: SRC dues amount $50 $35 refund semester

question: What is the process for hostel finance clearance?
answer: Before going to Finance for clearance, first confirm with the SCA office that your room has been booked. Finance will not process your clearance without a confirmed room booking. During orientation periods, SCA may be temporarily occupied — wait until they are free before visiting for clearance confirmation.
keywords: finance clearance hostel room booking SCA process orientation

question: When does the hostel room booking portal open?
answer: The hostel booking portal opens at 12:00 PM (noon) on the announced start date for each semester. All hostel residents are notified by email — check your email carefully for the exact date and link.
keywords: hostel booking portal open 12pm noon email semester

question: Who should new international students contact for help settling in?
answer: Level 100 international students can contact the International Students Representative on the ACSC, or reach out to the SCA office. The International Students Committee exists specifically to help you navigate campus challenges, accommodation, permits, and social integration. Don't be shy — they are approachable.
keywords: international student help support level 100 SCA ACSC representative

question: Where can international students stay during school vacation when the hostel closes?
answer: Accommodation during vacation is one of the biggest challenges for international students. If you are unsure where to stay when the hostel policy requires you to vacate, contact the International Students Representative as early as possible — they can help explore available options before the break.
keywords: hostel vacation policy accommodation break international student options

question: How do I vote in the ACSC student elections?
answer: To vote: (1) Log into ACity+ at acityplus.acity.edu.gh/student-login with your ACity Google account. (2) In the Courses tab, click the voting button at the top. (3) Select your candidates for each role and click Submit. You can only vote once and cannot change your selection. Voting windows typically run 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM on election day.
keywords: ACSC election vote voting portal ACity+ student login courses

question: What was the ACSC election timeline for 2026?
answer: 2026 ACSC Election dates: Vetting – Monday 16 March; Student Vetting – Tuesday 17 March; Election Day – Wednesday 25 March; Results Announcement – Thursday 26 March. For queries contact the Electoral Commission at ec@acity.edu.gh.
keywords: ACSC election 2026 dates timeline vetting results EC email

question: What ACSC committees can I join as a student?
answer: The ACSC recruits students for: Welfare Committee, Public Relations Committee, International Students Committee, Organizing Committee, Sports Committee, and Women's Committee. Applications open periodically — watch for announcements on the student WhatsApp groups and emails. A short vetting process is conducted as slots are limited.
keywords: ACSC committee join welfare PR sports women organizing international student

question: What services does the ACity library provide?
answer: The ACity library (librarian: Eric Amponsah) offers: e-library with academic textbooks for all courses, printing and scanning, Turnitin support, reference support, project work guidance, and fiction/novels. Students can visit to choose project topics, get help with academic writing, and access research databases. Authentic sources like the World Bank and African Development Bank are recommended over Google for research.
keywords: library services e-library printing Turnitin project reference librarian Eric Amponsah

question: Where is the counselor's office at ACity?
answer: The Counselor's Office is on the third floor of the main building — two floors above the library. It was relocated from the second floor. Students are welcome to walk in anytime for support.
keywords: counselor office location third floor above library wellbeing support

question: Where do I find my exam seating arrangement?
answer: Exam seating arrangements are published on the KOSI system. You will receive an email with subject 'Publication of Examination Time Table – Seating Arrangement on KOSI'. Log into KOSI and search 'seating chart'. It is uploaded the evening before or early morning (~7 AM) on exam day. Do NOT go to the hall looking for your name on a notice board — it will not be there. Any KOSI login issues must be fixed at the Registry before closing time on the day of the announcement.
keywords: exam seating arrangement KOSI system registry email notice board

question: What happens if I fail a mandatory course at ACity?
answer: You cannot progress academically if you fail a mandatory course. You will be required to resit or repeat the course before advancing. This policy was confirmed by the academic administration.
keywords: fail mandatory course progress resit repeat academic policy

question: Is course re-registration at ACity done online?
answer: Yes, the course re-registration process at ACity is fully online. You do not need to visit a physical office to register your courses for the semester.
keywords: re-registration online process courses register semester

question: How can I get legitimate software instead of pirated versions?
answer: If you are using pirated software and need the original licensed version, email Dr. Sena directly. The university has arrangements to help students access legitimate software at no cost. Don't use pirated software — the school will assist you.
keywords: software pirated original license Dr Sena email free

question: What is the Tech Center or MakeLab at ACity?
answer: The Tech Center (also called MakeLab or TEC) is ACity's innovation and maker space for hands-on projects, robotics, AI, and workshops. It is located on campus and hosts orientation sessions for new students (especially Level 100 / Class of 2029) at the start of each semester. Students can access equipment, attend events, and get support for tech-related academic projects.
keywords: Tech Center MakeLab TEC innovation maker space robotics Arduino Level 100 orientation

question: How can I listen to ACity Radio?
answer: ACity Radio streams live at https://zeno.fm/radio/acity-radio/ — accessible from any device. Programming includes the Morning Drive show, sports, relationship advice, academic discussions with faculty (Dr. Sena, the librarian, etc.), and student life content.
keywords: ACity Radio listen stream online zeno.fm morning drive

question: What are the Robotics Club membership dues?
answer: Robotics Club dues are GHC 10 per month, totalling GHC 40 per semester. Pay via Mobile Money to 0207483522 (Kweku Paapa Affadu-Danful). Dues help fund sessions, equipment maintenance, and Arduino kits for members.

question: What student clubs are active at ACity?
answer: Active clubs include: Robotics Club (MakeLab, weekly), Arts Media & Drama Club (U2, Tuesdays 6 PM), GDG on Campus (Google Developer Group, hackathons & workshops), ACity Christian Fellowship, Debate & Writing Club, Business Club, ACity Rotaract, TEDx Academic City, ACSC (student government), and ACity Radio. Most clubs welcome new members at the start of each semester.

question: What is the ACity+ student portal used for?

question: Are Tetr College of Business international students joining ACity campus?
answer: Yes — approximately 110 Tetr College of Business students from 40+ nationalities are joining ACity for a full semester, staying at Hostel B. This is part of ACity's global collaboration vision. ACity students can apply to serve as paid Student Buddies to help with their integration and campus tours.

question: What is the Hult Prize and can ACity students compete?
answer: The Hult Prize is a global student entrepreneurship competition where teams create solutions to major world challenges. The winning team receives $1 million USD to launch their social enterprise. ACity students can register at hultprize.org/register — it is a prestigious opportunity that boosts your CV and connects you with mentors and investors.

question: Where are food options on the ACity campus?
answer: On-campus dining options include Wafflemania (serves jollof, waakye, fried rice, fufu, spaghetti, and more — menu changes daily) and Yellow Bar. There are also student-run food vendors operating at various times. Menus and vendors may change each semester.

question: Does ACity have plans to build more student hostels?
answer: Yes, the university administration has confirmed there are plans to build additional hostels on campus to address accommodation demand, particularly for students who cannot be housed during vacations.
